# 1.2.93 - a server's uptime is no clock: the GM records take new entries after a restart, old time stamps read as unknown, and a trace's ring follows its record

Stage E90 ships with this version, alone. It repairs one fault measured at the owner's table on 31.10.2026 (Foundry 14.365
on The Forge, Daggerheart 2.6.5, the GM's browser). On a server whose clock counts from its start, the module's GM records
refused new entries after a restart: traces opened Daggerheart's own sheet and had no ring, and other GM records lost
entries the same way, until the server had run longer than the records' highest mark (about 1.6 hours of server time, set in
the session before the restart). 1.2.93 takes the server's
reading only where it is a date, and otherwise counts on the browser's own clock. 1 commit on 1.2.92 (248e798e), 71b726a6.
What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world.** No migration is added and nothing stored is rewritten at the update. New entries
   are kept from the first write after it. Entries that were refused while the records were cut off were never stored and
   cannot be brought back by the update (see "If entries were lost").
3. **What was wrong.** On the owner's server, `game.time.serverTime` read 2811317 beside `Date.now()` 1793415993407: the
   time since the server started, back near zero at each restart. The module took that number as its clock. The records'
   marks had been set in an earlier session of about 1.6 hours (5867475, the traces' 5868816, the highest 5869492), so after
   the restart every new entry carried a stamp under the marks and was dropped as older. The traces showed 0 alive and 31
   dead in `game.drpg.gmStoreStatus()`.

## At the table

### For the GM

- **The records take new entries again.** The module's clock and the records' clock take `game.time.serverTime` only when
  it reads as a date (1e12 milliseconds or more); otherwise they use the browser's own `Date.now()`. Every new stamp is above
  every stamp and mark stored under the old clock, so the records take writes with nothing migrated.
- **Old stamps read as unknown.** A time stamp written on the old clock is no longer read as a time 56 years ago:
  - The time of day: the HUD's minutes line prints no number for a start stamped on the old clock. The primary GM's browser
    writes such a time of day as begun now, with no pauses, at its ready and at an unpause.
  - The debate floor: a start stamped on the old clock reads as the moment this browser met it, so the debate has its whole
    time to run, and the primary GM's browser writes the start on the new clock at its next tick.
  - The trial clock: a trial whose start is stamped on the old clock shows no time line.
  - The take-back of a boundary crossed before the update is not offered (the stamp is far past the take-back window).
- **A trace's ring follows its record and its sight.** Since 1.2.91 a sight refresh no longer repaints tokens on a GM, and a
  change to the traces' record only nudged the icons, so a ring painted before its record, or while hidden, stayed that
  way. Now a change to the record repaints every trace token on the next frame, and a sight refresh paints only a visible
  trace or project token that shows no ring. A trace with no record waits for the next change to the record. On a slide of
  20 frames the sight pass ran 20 times and painted nothing (scenario 86, headless).
- **If entries were lost.** Nothing was stored for an entry written while its record refused it, and it was never sent to
  another GM, so none of those entries can be brought back; this holds for every record in that window (bullets, cast,
  ballots, verdict, observe, rolls and the others). Rows below the reset's own mark were taken by the reset, on purpose. For
  the traces, these exist:
  - `game.drpg.gmStoreHealth()` (and the primary GM's window at ready) counts the traces with no record: `traces` (nothing is
    left on the token; only a backup can help) and `tracesOnToken`.
  - `game.drpg.migrateRemnants()` (the window's "Move the traces into the ledger") writes a record from the token's flags,
    for the `tracesOnToken`. It writes a weak record (alive even on 1.2.92), and only for tokens that still carry their
    type flag. A Faint Prep trace's promotion is written at the world's upgrade mark, which on such a server may sit under
    the old cut, so that one field may not stand (read in the code, not measured).
  - `game.drpg.gmStoreReclaim("remnants")`, run on the GM browser that holds the old key from before 1.2.63, takes those
    rows again at their own stamps, which are above every old-clock cut (on 1.2.92 the same call clamped them under the
    cut). It restores the rows as they were at the upgrade to 1.2.63, for traces placed before it: edits since then are not in
    it, a row of a token deleted since comes back live too (harmless, its token is gone), and it cannot bring back any trace
    placed after 1.2.63.
  - `game.drpg.openRestoreDialog()`, with a case backup file if one exists (`gmStoreHealth()` shows when the last backup was
    made). A file made after the reset (5867475) and before the restart holds rows above the cut, which a plain restore takes.
    "Restore anyway the rows the last reset removed" fills rows at or under the cut with a fresh stamp, which on 1.2.93
    stands (on 1.2.92 it was dropped again); it also brings back what the reset removed on purpose, so use it only with a file
    whose rows you want.
  - A trace with none of these has no road back: nothing starts a record for an existing token that has none. Delete the
    trace and place it again (New trace).
- **On such a server each browser counts on its own clock.** The agreement between a player's and a GM's machine that
  1.2.92 had from the server's reading is gone on a server whose serverTime is an uptime; before this change two machines
  were measured 60 seconds apart (scenario 63 J1). A server whose serverTime is a date is unchanged.

### For players

- **No bridge action and no socket packet is added or changed** by this version. The clock a player's browser counts on follows
  the same rule: the server's reading where it is a date, the browser's own clock otherwise.

## Changed

- 16 files changed (+537, -31), one commit (`git show --stat 71b726a6`).
- **The clock:** `config.mjs` (`epochClock`, `isEpochStamp`, `staleStamp`), `utils.mjs` (`serverNow`), `gm-store.mjs` (the
  records' clock).
- **The readers of a stored stamp:** `hud.mjs` (`elapsedOf`, `readyPatch`, `unpausePatch`), `trial-floor.mjs` (`trialFloor`,
  `rebaseStaleFloor`), `trial-floor-ui.mjs` (`trialTime`). The readers that compare a stamp with another stamp, and the ask
  expiries, were judged and not changed.
- **The ring:** `remnant-ring.mjs` (`registerRemnantRings`), `perf-counters.mjs` (the counters `remnantRing.ledgerPass`,
  `.sightPass`, `.passPainted`).
- **Tests and books:** two numbered tests, R1564 and R1565, and three tier-2 tests, E90-T1 to E90-T3; scenario 61 gains A8;
  the harness can start a client on a server whose serverTime is an uptime; AUDIT 9.2 item 41 (LIVE-E04-01) is answered and
  item 348 (LIVE-E90-01) added; `tools/stages.json` gets the stage row.
- A tier-2 test that built a stamp from `game.time.serverTime` now builds it from the records' clock; on an uptime server
  that test had measured nothing.

## Known gaps

- **Carry-overs from the old clock.**
  - A trial running at the update shows no trial time on its console until it ends (its start is not rewritten).
  - The current time of day's summary loses its lines from before the primary GM's browser rewrote the start.
  - Between the update and the primary GM's ready, the HUD says the time of day has not started.
  - Old ask cards and the health check's dates show 1970 dates for stamps from the old clock (cosmetic).
- **Each browser on its own clock** on such a server (above).
- **Lost entries** cannot be brought back (above).
- **Harness only:** scenario 17 builds stamps from `game.time.serverTime` (lines 348, 644); with the uptime setting they would be
  older than the records' stamps. Not changed and not run here.
- **Not modelled:** a real server restart; a v14 server other than The Forge (whether its serverTime is a date is unknown,
  and such a server is unchanged by this version).
- **Not measured:** CI, the whole suite, the other scenarios and tier 2 as a whole.

## Checked

- Not checked in a real Foundry: a real server's restart, a v14 server other than The Forge, and two machines' clocks after
  the change (LIVE-E90-01, AUDIT 9.2 item 348). The restart is modelled by fake records (R1564) and a late GM on a server
  with an uptime clock (scenario 61 A8). The ring's frame cost on a real table is LIVE-E89-01's `fps()`.
- The fault, headless, at 248e798e before the change: `serverNow` and the records' clock read 2811317; a row under 5868816 and
  one after a simulated restart were dropped; the old key's row came back clamped under the cut; the HUD's minutes read
  1793411160409; the primary's ready wrote nothing; an unpause wrote a pause of 1793411999409 ms; the trial showed 29890193
  minutes used. After the change the same tests read as expected (R1564, R1565, E90-T1 to E90-T3, scenario 61 A8).
- Quick run at 248e798e plus the edits: lint, checks and gate ok; prose ok; tiers 0-1 697 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped, 0
  red; the stage's own tests 19 passed, 0 failed; scenarios 86 and 61 green (kept from the earlier run, not rerun after the
  last edits). The first run was red on one test-contract problem, fixed in the test.
- No local `npm test` result is cited, and CI has not run.
